title: deadeye config
description: Schema for ~/.deadeye/config.json (global) and .deadeye.json (project overlay). Both are optional; a missing file is equivalent to {}.

$schema.description: Optional pointer back to this schema, for editor validation/autocomplete. Ignored by deadeye itself.

effort.description: Effort-level guidance (Phase 2). Advisory only -- the Agent tool has no effort parameter to enforce, so there is no enforce mode.

preprocess.description: Context hygiene: Bash-output rewrite rules and unbounded-dump advisories, the duplicate-Read / large-Read / repeat-command / content-mode-Grep-without-head_limit advisories, the repeat-WebFetch / oversized-MCP-response / flag-escalation-retry / large-paste / long-exploration-streak / compact-timing advisories, the subagent brevity note, and response-size observation logging.

codemap.description: Cross-session codebase map: a directory/package skeleton rebuilt when the tracked-file list changes, plus accumulated touch-frequency and exploration notes, injected once per session. off disables both the SessionEnd writes and the injection.

update_check.description: Once-per-session background check for a newer deadeye release; when one is out, the agent asks (once per version) whether to update via /plugin update. Cached ~24h, never blocks the hook response. off disables the check and the ask.

routing_judge.description: When the cheap signals can't confidently place a subtask (the majority of real routing decisions), classify its complexity with a real model call (shells to `claude -p`, sonnet -- reuses your Claude login, no API key) instead of defaulting to the sonnet tier outright. Cached per task, fail-open on any error. A deliberate trade of the zero-network default for accuracy on genuinely ambiguous cases: this blocks the routing decision for up to 30s on an unsure, uncached task. off restores pure heuristics with no network call.

catalog_check.description: Background refresh of the hosted model/pricing catalog (a static JSON file on the project's GitHub Pages site), so a new model or price change reaches routing without a plugin release. Read-only GET, no request body. Cached ~24h, never blocks the hook response, and only ever takes effect if the fetched catalog is well-formed -- a bad or unreachable fetch always falls back to the compiled-in table, never breaks routing. A local ~/.deadeye/catalog.json override always wins over the hosted copy. off disables the fetch entirely.

tier_sample.description: Sample CONFIDENT high-tier routing decisions through the AI judge, which the live path never second-guesses (applyRoutingJudge only runs on an unsure decision). Exists to make over-routing visible: an escalation already biases routing UP, and nothing measured the other direction. Reports a judge-DISAGREEMENT rate, not an over-route rate -- an arbitrary production subtask has no grader, so the work can't be replayed and scored. Off by default because, unlike every other mode here, each sample spends a real `claude -p` call to buy measurement rather than a better answer for the call paying for it. See /deadeye-stats disagreement.

laya.description: Optional local Laya decision model (github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya, Apache 2.0), used for deadeye's typed decisions instead of a `claude -p` call. deadeye never installs, bundles, or supervises Laya -- you run `laya-serve` and set laya.endpoint; every call site falls back to its previous behavior on an unset endpoint, connection error, timeout, non-2xx, malformed JSON, or missing answer. A LADDER, not a switch, because Laya's untuned accuracy on typed decisions is 0.362 on its vendor's own eval against ~0.33 for a three-way guess, all figures vendor-self-reported: shadow asks and records but changes nothing; advise also annotates the visible decision reason; only authoritative lets an answer act. off (the default) never calls it and behaves exactly as releases before it existed. Setting this to off, or stopping laya-serve, or clearing laya.endpoint, or exporting DEADEYE_LAYA=off all disable it immediately. See /deadeye-laya and /deadeye-stats laya.

downshift_threshold.description: Minimum kernel confidence required to lower model tier or effort (INV-1). Upshifting is always free.

injection_budget_tokens.description: Ceiling on the total SessionStart advisory injection (INV-4).

disabled_rules.description: Rule/advisory names to disable individually: test-filter, build-filter, log-tail, diff-cap, lint-filter, install-filter, logs-tail, cat-large, history-cap, tf-plan-cap, kubectl-yaml-cap, npm-ls-cap, find-cap, tree-cap, du-cap, pkg-list-cap -- plus the non-Bash advisories grep-limit, read-advice, repeat-command, bash-retry, repeat-webfetch, mcp-oversize, large-paste, delegate-explore, and compact-timing -- plus the coder-mode security rules secret-literal, weak-crypto, tls-off, sql-concat, shell-interp, eval-dynamic, html-inject, java-deser, jwt-unverified, insecure-deser, cors-wildcard, cookie-insecure, weak-random-token, debug-on, ssti, xxe, open-redirect, nosql-inject, csrf-off, zip-slip, graphql-introspection, host-header-trust, dep-check (or a specific dep:<ecosystem>:<name>), and dep-flag (the session-start scan of existing manifests).

min_files.description: Working-tree modified/staged file count at which the gate's multi-file trigger fires.

default_level.description: Coder-mode intensity new sessions start at. spotter = flags the leaner alternative but builds what's asked; marksman = the lean-first ladder enforced (default); sniper = maximum minimalism, challenges the requirement itself. Switch mid-session with /deadeye-coder.

subagent_matcher.description: Optional regex on agent_type scoping which subagents receive the coder ruleset. Empty = all subagents. A regex that fails to compile fails open (injects).

injection_budget_tokens.description: Logged ceiling for the coder ruleset injection -- separate from the 400-token advisory budget, since the persona is an explicit opt-in and byte-stable per level.

security.description: Live security advisory on Edit/Write: SQL/shell/eval injection shapes, TLS-off, hardcoded secrets and provider tokens, weak crypto, and vulnerable/superseded dependencies in a manifest. "ask" additionally escalates a manifest edit that ADDS a dependency with a confirmed OSV advisory to a permission prompt (injection/secret/crypto findings stay advise). Independent of the coder persona level since 0.17.0 (turning the persona off no longer silences it) -- still disabled by security: "off", by /deadeye-mute, or by the DEADEYE=off / DEADEYE_CODER=off env kill switches.

security_osv.description: Whether the dependency check may consult OSV.dev (package name + version only, never file paths or code) via a background cache refresh. false keeps the check fully offline -- the bundled superseded-package table still works.

security.description: The exfiltration guard: watches PreToolUse/Read and /Bash for a credential file being read or shipped out. A top-level axis, independent of the coder persona -- not disabled by DEADEYE_CODER=off, only by DEADEYE=off.

exfil.description: On a match: ask escalates to a permission prompt the model can't answer for itself (a prompt-injected instruction can't approve it); advise emits a one-line nudge; off disables the guard. Default ask -- credential-file access is rare enough that interruptions should be too.

sensitive_paths.description: Extra glob patterns treated as sensitive credential paths, additive to the built-in table (~/.ssh private keys, ~/.aws/credentials, .env, ~/.claude/.credentials.json, ~/.netrc, ~/.kube/config, and more). Matched with filepath.Match against the full path and basename.

rate.description: Sample 1-in-N eligible decisions when mode.tier_sample is on. A value below 1 is read as the default rather than as 'every decision' -- a zero from a partial config file must not silently turn a paid sampler up to 100%. With mode.laya configured this stops being the cost control: the local classifier screens every eligible decision for free and only disagreements escalate to a paid confirmation.

endpoint.description: Base URL of a locally-run `laya-serve` (it binds 0.0.0.0:8000; deadeye talks to it over loopback, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8000). Empty means Laya is never called, whatever mode.laya says.

api_key_env.description: NAME of an environment variable holding laya-serve's bearer token -- never the token itself. laya-serve's LAYA_API_KEY is a credential, and a credential written into config.json is a secret at rest that `deadeye config` would print.

timeout_ms.description: Per-call deadline in milliseconds. Four call sites sit on the PreToolUse path that gates a real tool call, so this is deliberately generous enough for resident CPU inference (Laya is 193-464ms per call on CPU; the widely-quoted 32.8ms is a T4 GPU figure) and far too short for a cold checkpoint load, which costs seconds -- a server still loading loses the race and the call site falls back rather than stalling your tool call.

laya.description: Connection settings for the optional Laya decision model. See mode.laya.
